scope.summary: Give /settings/integrations the same sidebar sub-section list that /settings/general already has, so Skills, MCP, Voice dictation and Browser are reachable and trackable from the settings sidebar instead of only from the thread surface.
in: scroll-spy highlight and hash deep-link for those entries, reusing the existing generic code paths
out: new Integrations screen or sub-sections on mobile
changes to what the Integrations page itself renders

acceptance.case: First use: opening /settings/integrations shows four sub-entries under the Integrations nav item.
Sub-entry click scrolls to the matching section, or navigates with the hash when arriving from another page.
acceptance.note: handlePageSectionClick is path-generic; no per-page code.

acceptance.case: Reload and deep link: /settings/integrations#mcp lands on the MCP section.
Scroll-spy marks the visible sub-entry as active while scrolling.
acceptance.note: observedVisibilityScope now resolves for this path because it has page sections.

acceptance.case: Submenu never advertises a target that is not rendered.
acceptance.note: All four SettingsSection elements render unconditionally; only the Browser section's inner controls are gated by isElectron. A regression test in IntegrationsSettings.test.tsx pins the rendered section id set so the submenu cannot drift onto a missing target.

acceptance.case: Navigation away and unmount: submenu collapses with the existing Collapsible and the observer disconnects.
Compact/mobile web: sidebar closes on sub-entry click.

acceptance.note: Desktop wraps the web app; no separate change.
apps/mobile SettingsRouteScreen has no sub-section structure and no Integrations screen, so there is nothing to mirror.

acceptance.case: Server, contracts, providers, remote/relay and tunnel modes.
acceptance.note: Client-local static navigation data; nothing crosses the wire.
The submenu is display-only; it adds no toggle that needs an inverse.

implementation.notes: Purely additive: one new "/settings/integrations" key in the existing SETTINGS_PAGE_SECTIONS map in SettingsSidebarNav.tsx, same shape as the four keys already there. No component restructuring, no scroll-spy refactor, no shared type change, so upstream merges stay frictionless.

nextAction: None; slice complete pending maintainer review.
